doc.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021

title: Failing the conservatory audition and deciding to move to New York
summary: He missed the first conservatory audition, studied privately, got in, built a career in Australia, studied with Eddie Daniels and moved to New York in 2008 with no plan.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well was there a point, actually two points I’m going to ask about, that you thought oh I’d like to do this for a living, and then, but I have to go somewhere else to do this for a living?

So I could see doing this as a living, the light bulb moment that was the end of high school, and so then I went to audition for the conservatory of the music, which was the jazz, THE jazz course in Sydney. And the first year out of school I didn’t get in because I didn’t really know what I was doing, you know I think I kind of played a blues or something and I didn’t pass the audition because it was a very small intake and it was very competitive, and you know there’s a lot of great musicians. So I didn’t get in the first year. Then I started a psychology degree. On the side I started getting jazz lessons. I studied from a very hip graduate from that school and he kind of got me into a lot more stuff. We started playing Coltrane and Hank Mobley, and you know, getting into transcriptions. So he kind of got me on the right path. And then the next year I got into music school. So that was kind of how I got into the conservatory. My, I suppose the next significant step — coming to New York — that happened in 2008. So I’d been out of college maybe ten years and I had a good career in Australia, did a lot of great commercial work, great jazz work, but it was, as you could probably imagine, a very small market. In the meantime I actually came over to the States a few times to study with Eddie Daniels, because he’s a huge influence on me, I mean I love Eddie, he’s incredible. But a year before moving here I came to visit New York and I kind of checked it out and checked out all the clubs and got some lessons. And I went home and I was so inspired, it was just like, it just filled me. And then I came to the awful realization that if I don’t move over here I’ll regret it. So a couple of months after being home I was like okay, I’ve just got to do this. I don’t know what I’m going to do but I’ve just got to come over. So I started to work on a Visa, that took a few months. And pretty much 12 months after visiting I moved over here for good. So I’ve been here 12 years now. And that was it. Didn’t have a plan.
